sources.title: Combining Double Sampling and Bounds to Address Nonignorable Missing Outcomes in Randomized Experiments
sources.authors: Alexander Coppock; Alan S. Gerber; Donald P. Green; Holger L. Kern

local_copy.path: docs/papers/Combining Double Sampling and Bounds to Address Nonignorable Missing Outcomes in Randomized Experiments Coppock(2017).pdf

inspected_anchors: Sections2.1–2.4,pages190–195: randomized treatment, outcome stability, selective follow-up response and equations1–16.
Section2.5,pages195–197: sample-ratio endpoints, analytic variance and asymptotic true-ATE coverage, equations17–24.
Section2.6: poststratification; Section2.7,pages198–199:delta mixture restriction on nonresponders, equations28–29.
Sections3–5: response-rate versus sample-size distinction, original application and limits.
supported_claims: Random follow-up combined with bounded outcomes supplies partial identification under outcome stability despite selective completion.
Published sensitivity delta restricts nonresponse mixture, not change in the recovered historical outcome.
The published confidence target is asymptotic true-ATE coverage, distinct from the authored finite-sample whole-set claim.
scope: Primary theory read; no reproduction of the original application or generalization to bank data.
An acquired2016appendix has a different listed author set; its identity is preserved separately and it is not cited as the2017article.

sources.title: attrition: Addressing Nonignorable Attrition with Double Sampling and Bounds
inspected_anchors: DESCRIPTION version, GPL-3 declaration and outcome-stability wording.
Full277-line estimators source: double-sampling combination, bootstrap accounting and trimming branches.
User-facing lines1–145,300–345,548–645: input mapping, selection target and delta definition.
supported_claims: The inspected implementation uses follow-up response ratios and analytic variance before a normal critical-value inversion.
Actual delta code and function documentation implement the paper nonresponse mixture and cannot repair changed outcomes when completion is full.
The trimming interface targets always-reporters, a different estimand, and separately declares selection assumptions.
GPL-3 is a package declaration, not evidence of qualified integration or resolved dependency permissions.
scope: Static inspection only; no downloaded code executed.
No native performance, interface qualification, package coverage or correctness beyond inspected algebra claimed.
